title: unified.app_instance.requested payload
description:
Published by AbeonUnified when an organisation is given an application (ADR-0031 §5). A business application runs as one deployment per client, so this is the order for one: create the database, deploy the image, route `host + path` to it.

The provisioner is part of the deployment layer, not of the platform services — nothing here knows how a deployment is made. It answers by marking the assignment `ready` or `failed` through the internal registry API, and the application appears in the launcher only then.

At-least-once like every event (ADR-0002): a provisioner must treat a repeat for a pair it has already built as the no-op it is, not as a second deployment.

The file name is the routing key.

org_id.description: The organisation the instance belongs to. Also the envelope's `org_id`.

app.description: The application's name in the catalogue, which is also the first segment of its permissions (ADR-0001).

host.description: The client's host, from Auth's organisation record (ADR-0031 §2).

path.description: The path prefix the instance is served under on that host, e.g. `/cms`. Null when the catalogue has none, which a provisioner should treat as the root.

public_host.description: The host this instance serves its public surface from, when it has one (ADR-0033) — the client's own domain for a website a CMS publishes, read by people with no account. Absent for an application that is only a panel. The provisioner routes it to the same instance as `host` + `path`, with no prefix.

slug.description: The organisation's slug, for naming databases and deployments legibly.
